title: Sobhana Mostary Marks 100th Cap With Top Score as Bangladesh Open Asia Cup
excerpt: The Bangladesh batter scored 40 in her milestone match and recalled how the 2018 Asia Cup triumph over India transformed women's cricket in her country.
body:
• Bangladesh beat Indonesia by 71 runs in their Women's Asia Cup 2026 opener in Dubai, bowling the debutants out for 58
  • Sobhana Mostary top-scored with 40 in her 100th international match, while Nahida Akter took 3 for 15 and Marufa Akter finished with 2 for 6
  • Mostary told the Times of India that Bangladesh's 2018 Asia Cup triumph over India "changed everything" for women's cricket in the country, bringing greater facilities and financial support
  • Bangladesh are in Group B with Sri Lanka, Indonesia, and UAE, and can only meet India in the knockout stages

Sobhana Mostary marked her 100th international appearance with a top score of 40 as Bangladesh beat Indonesia by 71 runs in their Women's Asia Cup 2026 opener at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.

Bangladesh posted 129 for 8 before bowling Indonesia — making their Asia Cup debut — out for 58, with left-arm spinner Nahida Akter claiming Player of the Match honors for her figures of 3 for 15.

A Milestone Knock Under Pressure

Mostary anchored the Bangladesh innings through a middle period where runs were difficult to come by. After openers Juairiya Ferdous (8) fell early to a sharp catch by Ni Ariani off Ni Made Putri Suwandewi, Mostary and Dilara Akter (27 off 31) built a steady partnership that took Bangladesh to 58 for 2 at the halfway mark.

""After 2018, we beat India and won the Asia Cup, so it was a huge change in Bangladesh women's cricket."

Indonesia's spinners kept Bangladesh in check, with the batters managing only a handful of boundaries through the middle overs. Mostary struck the first six of the innings in the 13th over, but the momentum shifted when 16-year-old debutant legspinner Sofia Velic dismissed captain Nigar Sultana. Ni Luh Dewi then struck twice in the 17th over to remove Mostary for 40 and Ritu Moni in quick succession.

Shorna Akter's 31 off 18 balls injected late urgency, but Bangladesh lost five wickets for 21 runs in the final 17 balls. Ni Ariani finished with 3 for 28 as Indonesia's bowlers produced a spirited showing to limit the damage.

Indonesia Bowled Out on Debut

The target of 130 proved far too steep for Indonesia on their first Asia Cup appearance. Marufa Akter set the tone with figures of 2 for 6 from three overs, including a maiden, while Nahida Akter's left-arm spin proved virtually unplayable. Indonesia were bowled out for 58 in 17.3 overs, handing Bangladesh a comfortable 71-run victory.

The Win That Changed Everything

Ahead of the tournament, Mostary spoke to the Times of India about the significance the Asia Cup holds for Bangladesh women's cricket. She recalled how their 2018 triumph — when Bangladesh beat India twice, including in a dramatic final in Kuala Lumpur that went down to the last ball — transformed the sport in her country.

"After 2018, we beat India and won the Asia Cup, so it was a huge change in Bangladesh women's cricket. Everything changed. They started giving us lots of facilities, money, everything. There was a lot of change."

In that 2018 final, Jahanara Alam completed the winning two runs as Bangladesh chased down India's 112 for 9 by three wickets. The Bangladesh Cricket Board announced a 2-crore taka reward for the team. For Mostary, the legacy of that victory drives the current squad's ambitions.

"We think this Asia Cup, we fight for the title, because if we beat India, so maybe we own the Asia Cup."

A Journey of Patience

Mostary's own path has been defined by persistence. She started playing cricket at age 10 when her father took her to a village academy. After six months of training, she was selected by the Bangladesh Krira Shiksha Pratisthan (BKSP) and moved to Dhaka alone to pursue the sport. Her international debut came at just 16, but a regular place in the XI did not follow immediately.

"It was very difficult. I always travelled with the team, but couldn't play. I just waited and thought that someday the opportunity would come and I could show my strength," she said.

The patience has paid off. Mostary named India captain Harmanpreet Kaur as her childhood idol, specifically recalling Kaur's unbeaten 171 against Australia at the 2017 Women's World Cup. She described playing India as "very interesting and always very exciting," and picked Deepti Sharma as the Indian bowler she most admires.

Bangladesh next face Sri Lanka on September 6 in Group B. A meeting with India can only come in the knockout stages, but if Mostary's words are any indication, Bangladesh will be ready for it.
